title: How can one angle of a rhombus give the other three?
description: One angle of a rhombus is fifty degrees. The diagonal cuts the corners into four equal angles, and the angle sum of a triangle finds each of them. Keeko doubts that equal sides give equal angles.
teaching_notes: One idea: a diagonal of a rhombus makes four equal angles, so the angle sum of one triangle gives all of them. Watch for students who think equal sides mean equal angles.

source: Rhombus ABCD has ∠A = 50°. Find its other angles.
video_script.why: The child sees that the diagonal splits the rhombus into equal angles, so one angle sum finds the rest.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rhombus ABCD with angle A = 50 degrees
video_script.anchor: the rhombus ABCD of the book with angle A = 50 degrees and the diagonal BD
video_script.wrong_answer: all four angles are fifty degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks equal sides mean equal angles, so every angle is fifty degrees, but two corners are wide and two are sharp.
video_script.payoff_line: Angle B and angle D are one hundred thirty degrees each

final_answer.spoken: angle B is one hundred thirty degrees, angle C is fifty degrees, and angle D is one hundred thirty degrees

never_show: all four angles written as 50 degrees
maths_rules: the diagonal BD makes four equal angles x, two at B and two at D
in triangle ADB: x + x + 50 = 180, so 2x = 130 and x = 65
angle C = angle A = 50, opposite angles of a parallelogram
video_script.design: One idea: the diagonal gives four equal angles, so one triangle finds them all. One rhombus stays on the board with the diagonal drawn in.

<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find angle B, angle C and angle D.

Call each of them x.

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, look at triangle eigh D B.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Its angles add up to one hundred eighty, so x plus x plus fifty is one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Two x is one hundred thirty, so x is sixty five degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='b'/>Step three, angle B is made of two angles x.
Sixty five plus sixty five is one hundred thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Angle D is the same.

marks.c: angle C is matched with angle A
marks.chk: the four angles are added to three hundred sixty

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step four, opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
A rhombus is a parallelogram, so angle C equals angle eigh, which is fifty degrees.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check, fifty plus one hundred thirty plus fifty plus one hundred thirty is three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Angle B and angle D are one hundred thirty degrees each.
Angle C is fifty degrees.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: four angles of fifty degrees crossed out; the rhombus with two sharp corners and two wide corners

marks.doubt: fifty degrees is written at all four corners
marks.look: two corners glow as sharp and two as wide
marks.fix: the four angles are crossed out and the true angles written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks all four angles are fifty degrees, because all four sides are equal.
<bookmark mark='look'/>But look at the shape. Two corners are sharp, and two are wide.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Equal sides do not make equal angles. Only opposite angles are equal.
